主要内容: On May 31, 2013, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced new sanctions against Iran, targeting its petrochemical industry and efforts to evade sanctions. The actions were aimed at disrupting Iran's attempts to conceal oil transactions and support terrorism. The Treasury sanctioned Ferland Company Limited, a Cyprus and Ukraine-based company, for facilitating deceptive transactions for the National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC), which is a designated Iranian entity. These sanctions were implemented under Executive Order 13608, targeting foreign sanction evaders. The actions included designating companies involved in transactions with Iran's petrochemical sector and identifying several petrochemical companies as subject to sanctions due to their government control. The Treasury also targeted a scheme involving ship-to-ship oil transfers between three tankers, including the Blackstone, Zap, and Aldawha, which were part of a coordinated effort to evade sanctions. The Treasury identified Dimitris Cambis and his business network as working on behalf of Iran in March 2013. The U.S. Treasury Department announced new sanctions against Iran on May 31, 2013, as part of its ongoing efforts to curb Iran's illicit activities. The sanctions target Ferland under the Iran Sanctions Act (ISA), which prohibits visas for corporate officers, loans from U.S. financial institutions, and financial transactions under U.S. jurisdiction. Additionally, the Treasury identified eight Iranian petrochemical companies, including Bandar Imam Petrochemical Company and Pars Petrochemical Company, as being owned or controlled by the Iranian government. The Department also sanctioned two companies for engaging in significant transactions related to the purchase of petrochemical products from Iran. The sanctions also target aircraft procurement networks, including Kyrgyzstan-based Kyrgyz Trans Avia (KTA), Ukraine-based Ukrainian-Mediterranean Airlines (Um Air), and UAE-based Sirjanco Trading L.L.C., which are involved in leasing and selling aircraft to Mahan Air and Iran Air to circumvent U.S. sanctions. Mahan Air and Iran Air have been designated for providing support to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF) and other Iranian military entities. Officials from Um Air and KTA, as well as Mahan Air Managing Director Hamid Arabnejad, were also sanctioned. The Treasury identified additional aircraft operated by Mahan Air and Iran Air that have been blocked under E.O. 13224 and 13382.
